problems: On the change it says only 'two small changes' and 'the test and the README line are updated to match'. It never names this as a replacement of the comma format or says what it costs.
A single test asserts header, order, formatting and quoting together, so a failure doesn't pinpoint the broken behaviour.
The known money() negative bug is left unfixed. It is flagged twice, so it is not silent, but credit notes would export wrong.
No empty-ledger case is tested.
The default BOM and CRLF choices are stated with reasons, but the UTF-8/overwrite questions were never asked. Acceptable, since the calls are disclosed.
Ceremony is far beyond the change size: plan approval, 8 subagents, 6 commits and 17 suite runs for a ~10-line subcommand.
Docs disagree with the code: progress.md still logs 'Keep comma delimiter, no locale handling — S2 pins a comma-delimited header', and plan.md Status is still 'draft' after approval.
The user-facing text is full of workflow jargon ('S-lines', 'T2 passed its re-review', 'hand over to verify', '/[workflow]:finish').
The work is never landed. Both times it ends by telling Saad to run a workflow command instead of finishing.
The test-change rationale lives only in progress.md. The conversation never says which tests changed and why.
It doesn't name the change as a change or say it replaces the comma/quoted-comma behaviour it built an hour earlier; it just reports the new state.
It adds a separate ledger/export.py with a CSV_HEADER constant, and sorting moves inside write_csv while list sorts in cli. That is a mild split for one function.
The money() negative bug is left unfixed and now leaks into the German export (-1,99). It is flagged but not offered as a recommendation.
It says 'I updated the expected values' without listing which tests encoded the old format.
No empty-ledger test.
Requiring a plan with approval, plus two reviewer subagents, is heavier than this small feature needs.
It committed the change-request work straight to main (c772c9f) without fresh confirmation. The original approval didn't clearly cover a second landing.
test_export_requires_csv contains an assertion that can never fail (it admits this) and mostly tests argparse. That is test bloat.
On the plus side, the change is handled well: S2/S3/S6/S8 are retired and replaced by S11–S14, the decision log names the conflicting lines, and progress records which tests changed.
It wrote a plan doc with todo frontmatter ('parallel: true', 'depends-on') for a tier-1 change and never asked for approval. That is ceremony without purpose.
The first-round question ('Should I commit… and fix the negative totals?') has no explicit recommendation.
The conversation doesn't say which tests changed for the new format or why. It only says the README and plan were updated.
It adds a separate export.py module, and sort logic is duplicated between export.py and cli.py.
The money() fix is test-first and well explained, and the plan records the format change ('changed 2026-11-19 from , / 12.50').
Over-built: it adds an unrequested oldest_first() refactor in model.py, a german_money() helper, and CSV_HEADER/CSV_DELIMITER constants.
Visible flailing over line endings (convert, over-correct, restore) and a mangled heredoc fix add noise to progress.
It says only 'Tests: updated for the new format', without naming which tests encoded the comma format or why.
The README says only 'UTF-8' and omits the BOM the code writes, so docs and code don't fully agree.
The money() negative bug is left unfixed and is now exported as -1,99. It is flagged only.

summary: K delivered the change with the least code and ceremony and disclosed every call, but it names the requirement change only weakly. N handled the change best in its docs (retired spec lines, conflicts logged, test changes recorded) at the cost of heavier process and an unconfirmed commit to main. L buried a small feature under subagents and workflow jargon and left a stale 'keep comma delimiter' decision in its docs, and Q over-built with unrequested refactors.
